newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters to launch new German indicator.
newsitem.headline: Reuters to launch new German indicator.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc and the German Association for Materials Management, Purchasing and Logistics (BME) will present a new leading indicator for the German economy at a news conference on Tuesday.

The German Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) index will be published monthly and is based on a survey of 350 companies carried out exclusively for Reuters by research group NTC Publications Ltd in cooperation with the BME.
The PMI is a composite index designed to provide an overall view of activity in the manufacturing economy and acts as a leading indicator for Europe's largest economy.
It is modelled on the closely watched U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index.
Copyright in the BME/Reuters Purchasing Managers' Index is owned by Reuters Limited.
A similar index calculated by NTC in Britain has established itself as a respected indicator of economic trends there since it was launched in July 1991, analysts say.

"It's a very important piece of statistical information for the market. I'm sure it's one of many indicators watched by policymakers," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy in London.
"There was a fair degree of scepticism initially but the index has become part of the statistical landscape."
The German PMI surveys materials, purchasing and logistics managers and the findings are weighted by region, sector and number of employees.
The indicator is derived from individual diffusion indices which measure changes in output, new orders, employment, suppliers' delivery times and stocks of goods purchased.
A reading of the PMI below 50 percent indicates that the manufacturing economy is generally declining, while a level above 50 percent shows it generally expanding.
The more the index deviates from 50, the greater the improvement or decline in the economic situation in the current month.
A seasonally adjusted index will also be provided but that will be subject to revision as each month's new data will improve the assessment of seasonal adjustments.
As a rule the index will be published on the first stock market trading day of the month on Reuters news systems. The first index will cover April 1997 and will be published on May 6 at 0730 GMT.
It will be released alongside PMI data running back to April 1996.
